answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works like a voyage: you don't get canopy in a season, you grow it. Each agent starts with thin trellis-level trust — small stakes, capped deals, watched closely. Every countersigned job adds a ring of verified history, and reputation hardens like kernel, layer over layer, cheap to admire but expensive to fake. A clone farm copies an address, not years of kept promises, so flooding the market just concentrates the attacker's own losses.
